high.title: Oil Price Surge: Stocks "Hard to Digest", This Investment Channel Benefits Greatly
high.summary: Global oil prices continue to escalate, surpassing $100/barrel amid ongoing Middle East tensions, raising concerns about a new energy shock for the global economy. FIDT's Deputy Director Bui Van Huy warns of an emerging negative scenario with Brent crude maintaining above $80/barrel, reflecting supply disruption risks in prolonged geopolitical instability. This drives global inflationary pressures, forcing central banks, especially the Fed, to delay interest rate cuts or potentially signal tightening if prices continue climbing. In this scenario, the USD tends to strengthen with DXY surpassing 100, creating additional pressure on emerging markets. For Vietnam, USD/VND faces clear upward pressure, potentially pushing deposit interest rates to 7-8% range. This development is critical for VND traders as it suggests sustained FX pressure and potential monetary policy responses from SBV.

high.title: Big Money About to "Land" in the Market, SSI Research Names 30 Stocks Attracting Strongest Capital
high.summary: Next week, Vietnam's stock market will receive crucial information as FTSE announces its mid-term review results (expected morning of April 8, 2026). This is considered a pivotal test in Vietnam's upgrade roadmap. SSI Research evaluates that Vietnam remains on track for emerging market upgrade according to FTSE Russell standards in 2026, with an estimated $1.67 billion in passive capital flows from global ETFs. If passing this review, the market could begin attracting passive fund flows from September 2026. VIC is forecasted to attract the highest capital inflow of around $414 million, followed by HPG with about $147 million, while VHM and FPT also rank among leaders. This represents a major catalyst for Vietnamese equities and the VND, as successful FTSE upgrade would bring substantial foreign capital inflows and boost market credibility.

high.title: One Bank Lists 10%/Year Deposit Interest Rate
high.summary: PVComBank lists deposit rates ranging from 4.75% to 10%/year for retail customers in early April, up from the previous month. The highest rate of 10%/year applies to certain long-term deposits with specific balance requirements. Standard retail deposits show: 1-3 weeks at 0.50%/year, 1-5 months at 4.75%/year, 6-11 months at 5.50%/year, and notably 12-13 months at elevated rates reaching 10%/year for large deposits. This represents a significant increase in deposit rates, reflecting potential monetary tightening pressures. For VND traders and bond investors, this signals that Vietnamese banks are competing aggressively for deposits, potentially indicating liquidity tightening or preparation for higher policy rates from SBV. Such high deposit rates could pressure government bond yields upward and suggest VND strength may be needed to maintain competitive rates.

medium.title: One Decision Will Put Vietnam on Par with China, India
medium.summary: After London stock exchange closes on April 7 (early morning April 8 Vietnam time), FTSE Russell will announce market classification review results. If passing this crucial test, Vietnam will officially be upgraded to Secondary Emerging market status, ranking alongside China, India, Egypt, Indonesia. Vietcap estimates 0% probability of Vietnam failing this review based on Ministry of Finance's Circular 08/2026 removing final technical barriers for international index funds.

medium.title: Signals of Bottom Formation Appear, Vietcap Forecasts VN-Index Could Conquer 1,830 Points in April
medium.summary: Vietcap views the market entering April with mixed opportunities and risks, as valuations have become more attractive after sharp corrections but capital flows remain cautious. VN-Index P/E has retreated below 10-year median to around 15.2x after March decline. The FTSE Russell mid-term review on April 8 regarding Vietnam's market upgrade remains a key catalyst.

medium.title: Capital Flows Stirring to Return, SSI Research Names 13 Stocks About to Enter New "Wave"
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market entered 2026 with positive momentum, quickly approaching the base target of 1,920 points in early months before entering correction in March. SSI Research attributes this mainly to profit-taking after hot growth period, along with concerns about rising domestic interest rates and increasing geopolitical instability. However, the correction is more tactical than structural while medium-term market prospects remain supported by multiple factors.

medium.title: Many Banks Plan to Pay Dividends, Bonus Shares in 2026, Highest Rate Up to Over 31%
medium.summary: Major banks announce substantial dividend and bonus share plans for 2026. MB plans 25% total dividend (15% stock, 10% cash), ACB targets 20% total (13% stock, 7% cash), VPBank also plans significant payouts. These high dividend yields from banking sector could support investor interest and potentially strengthen VND through reduced share supply and attractive returns.
